collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined ground truth listing every Wikidata-declared notable work of each Nobel Prize in Literature laureate from prize-years 2000 through 2024, with the laureate's Nobel year, the work's publication year, and the laureate's primary writing language. The 25-laureate universe is source-defined by Wikidata's P166 (award received) + P585 (point in time qualifier) for Q37922 (Nobel Prize in Literature). Per-laureate works are every Wikidata P800 (notable work) value declared on the laureate's item, with publication years from each work's P577. Per-laureate work count varies from 1 (J. M. Coetzee) to 10 (Jon Fosse) and reflects Wikidata's curation depth rather than a curator-imposed cap; this is honest source-defined behavior.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (Wikidata SPARQL endpoint): universe + value (defines the 25-row laureate universe via P166/P585 and the 125-row work universe via P800 after the documented post-processing; supplies Laureate name via rdfs:label, Nobel Year via P585, Work via P800/rdfs:label, and Publication Year via P577)
- source_urls[1] (List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Literature): entity-detail + value (supplies the per-laureate Original Language column; for laureates with multiple writing languages, the article lists them in priority order and the staged value is the first language listed)

No separate validation source. The Wikidata snapshot is the universe-defining grounded artifact. The Wikipedia article is used only to fill the Original Language column; this attribute is not in Wikidata's schema in a 1-laureate-1-language form (P1412 'languages spoken/written' is multi-valued and includes secondary languages; P103 'native language' diverges from writing language for some laureates). The Wikipedia laureate list's Language(s) column is the canonical source for primary writing language across the literary canon and is what the staged Original Language reflects.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass. Universe (25 Nobel Literature laureates 2000-2024) is fully source-defined via Wikidata P166/P585. Partition rule (per laureate) is source-defined. Per-laureate work selection is fully source-defined via Wikidata P800 — variable count per laureate, ranging from 1 to 10 — rather than curator judgment.
- Seed/provenance: original instance, not derived from a seed in example_questions.txt. The picker recommended an original implicit_join because no untouched seed fits cleanly (#8 fails the viability gate, #12 fails the viability gate, #9 is set_operation rather than implicit_join).
- Category: implicit_join (gap 5, the lone largest gap among the 15 categories) primary. The DB-analog shape is a join of the laureate set with each laureate's notable-work table on Wikidata, taking every notable work per laureate. Secondary multi_attribute_projection because the per-row structure also tests per-cell calibration over (Work, Publication Year, Original Language).
- Source plan: Tier A Wikidata SPARQL primary + Tier B Wikipedia article for the per-laureate Original Language column; gt_construction = sparql_wikidata; source_count = 2.
- Expected shape: ~125 rows x 5 columns; composite PK (Laureate, Work).
- Domain: Culture/Literature — new subdomain in the saturated Culture family (Culture currently has Film x3, Music x1, Gaming x1; Literature is unrepresented at the subdomain level).
- Risks/adaptation: Wikidata's P800 coverage is uneven across laureates (Coetzee 1, Tokarczuk 11, Fosse 10), reflecting editorial curation depth on Wikidata rather than a per-laureate factual cap. The audit flagged the prior 3-per-laureate hand-selection as not source-reproducible; the current Wikidata-based universe replaces curator judgment with a deterministic SPARQL extraction.
- Decision: Stage.

Why original rather than seed-driven: the picker (2026-04-30 evening snapshot) flagged implicit_join (gap 5) as the lone largest-gap category. The remaining seeds in example_questions.txt that nominally target implicit_join all fail the fast viability gate (seed #8 and #12 produce empty row sets; seed #9 is set_operation). With no usable seed, an original implicit_join was the right pick per workflows.md step 2(b).

Category <-> operation_type pairing: query_category=implicit_join pairs canonically with operation_type=join per references/artifact-contract.md. The structural primitive being tested is the join of the laureate set with each laureate's bibliography table.

Domain selection: Culture/Literature is a new subdomain in the Culture family (which previously had Culture/Film x3, Culture/Music, Culture/Gaming). Adding Literature broadens the Culture family rather than concentrating in Film. Per the 2026-04-30 picker snapshot, Culture is one of the larger families but Literature was unrepresented within it.

Post-audit (2026-04-30): the prior staging used a curator-judgment 3-works-per-laureate hand-selection from each laureate's Wikipedia article 'Notable works' infobox row or 'Selected bibliography' section. The audit flagged this as not source-reproducible because each laureate's Wikipedia article often surfaces 4-6 plausible candidate works and the 3-per-laureate selection was curator judgment (e.g., Kazuo Ishiguro's article lists 5 notable works in the infobox; the prior staging chose 3). The repaired instance replaces the hand-selection with a fully deterministic SPARQL extraction over Wikidata's P800 (notable work) statements; per-laureate work count is now variable from 1 to 10 and is exactly what Wikidata declares. The post-audit row count went from 75 (25 × 3) to 125 (deterministic, after dropping 3 unresolved-QID rows and deduping (Laureate, Work) on MIN year for works with multiple P577 statements). The audit's non-blocking hygiene item — clarifying Original Language for multi-language laureates such as Gao Xingjian — is addressed by stating in normalization_decisions that the staged Original Language is the FIRST language listed by the master Wikipedia laureate-list article for each laureate (Chinese for Gao, who also writes in French; English for Ishiguro; Russian for Belarus-based Alexievich; etc.).
normalization_decisions: Universe definition: laureates are every entity with a Wikidata P166 (award received) statement whose value is Q37922 (Nobel Prize in Literature) and whose P585 (point in time) qualifier names a year between 2000 and 2024 inclusive. Works are every value of each laureate's P800 (notable work) statements at the time of the snapshot. Publication Year normalization: P577 datetimes are truncated to a 4-digit year; for works whose Wikidata item lacks P577, the staged Publication Year is the explicit sentinel 'not specified' (8 rows, matching the precedent set by top_10_most_populous_cities_per_continent). When a work has multiple P577 statements (Wikidata occasionally records different editions/printings/translations as separate statements), the staged Publication Year is MIN(year) across statements, which corresponds to first publication. One such work in the staged set: Louise Glück's 'Faithful and Virtuous Night' has two P577 = 2020 statements; the dedup rule yields a single row with Publication Year = 2020. Three rows whose Work label is an unresolved QID (e.g., 'Q120560612' for one Mo Yan work whose Wikidata label service returned a QID rather than a label) are dropped; these are Wikidata data-completeness issues rather than query bugs and are documented as a known scope limitation in _extraction_notes. Laureate name normalization: three rdfs:label values are mapped to the master Nobel-list canonical form to keep the Laureate column consistent with the Wikipedia laureate list — 'Vidiadhar Surajprasad Naipaul' to 'V. S. Naipaul', 'John Maxwell Coetzee' to 'J. M. Coetzee', and 'Jean-Marie Gustave Le Clézio' to 'J. M. G. Le Clézio'. Original Language normalization (post-audit hygiene fix): the staged Original Language is the laureate's PRIMARY writing language as listed by the Wikipedia 'List of Nobel laureates in Literature' article's Language(s) column, taking the FIRST language when multiple are listed. Specifically: Gao Xingjian writes in Chinese and French; the staged value is Chinese (first listed). Doris Lessing writes in English regardless of country origin (UK/Iran). Kazuo Ishiguro writes in English regardless of birth country (Japan). Svetlana Alexievich writes in Russian regardless of country of citizenship (Belarus). Han Kang writes in Korean. Le Clézio writes in French regardless of country (France/Mauritius). For all 25 laureates the master list's first-language entry matches the language each laureate is canonically associated with for the literary canon. Work title normalization: titles are verbatim from Wikidata's English rdfs:label without stripping diacritics or accent marks (e.g., 'Le Procès-Verbal' for Le Clézio, 'La Place de l'Étoile' for Modiano).
open_questions: 1. Whether the variable per-laureate work count (1 for Coetzee, 10 for Fosse, 11 staged for Tokarczuk before the QID drop) reflects benchmark-relevant signal or Wikidata-curation noise; a future v2 could renormalize by capping at, e.g., the laureate's first 5 P800 entries by publication year. 2. Whether Bob Dylan's 7 P800 works (mostly songs and albums rather than books) should be excluded as a special case; the current design includes them because Wikidata's P800 declarations are part of the source-defined universe and Dylan's Nobel was for songwriting. 3. Whether Original Language should come from a per-work attribute (e.g., P407 language of work) rather than a per-laureate attribute; the current design uses a per-laureate language because most laureates write only in one language and Wikidata's per-work P407 has thinner coverage. 4. Whether the 8 'not specified' Publication Year sentinels should be back-filled from each work's individual Wikipedia article (where one exists) rather than left at the Wikidata-only sentinel; the current design accepts the sentinel to keep the instance as a clean Tier A primary source plus a single Tier B language column.
